---
title: "Loading/Viewing my Data"
---
```{r}
#| include: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
```

There are many different ways of viewing a dataset 

```{r}
data("penguins") #loading the penguins dataset that is included in R
```

glimpse() shows all of the variables and their R variable type

```{r}
glimpse(penguins)
```
\
head() takes the top 6 rows from the dataset and displays it like a normal table, tail() does the same from the bottom

```{r}
head(penguins)
```
\

nrow() and ncol() will tell you how many rows and columns respectively are in the data

```{r}
nrow(penguins) #Returns the number of rows in the penguins data
```

```{r}
ncol(penguins) #Returns the number of columns
```

\

## Reading in Data

To read in data from a file, your code depends on what kind of file it is

You can use read_csv() to load .csv files

```{r}
#| eval: false
read_csv("mydataset.csv") #Example for reading in a csv file called mydataset
```
